akimbo.e: From Middle English in kenebowe, in kene bowe (“in a keen bow”, i.e. “in a sharp bend or angle”), from in (“in”) + keen, kene (“brave, keen, sharp”) + bowe (“bow, bend”). Alternately, possibly from Old Norse kengr (“bent”) + bogi (“a bow”), compare Icelandic kengboginn (“bow-bent”).

s.d: (used of arms and legs) bent outward with the joint away from the body
x: a tailor sitting with legs akimbo

s.d: With a crook or bend; with the hand on the hip and elbow turned outward.
x: "Now, then, mister," said he, with his head cocked and his arms akimbo, "what are you driving at? Let's have it straight, now."
Girls take hold of the skirts; boys place the hands akimbo, bend forward from the waist, and bow.

s.d: With legs spread and the knees bent in an outward or awkward way, sometimes with the feet touching.
with hands on hips and elbows extending outward
Into, in, or of the position where the arms are akimbo.
x: Otherwise, it is likely that she may be accosted as "dear" or "Sally,"—invited to take "a drop o' tea," or otherwise chaffed by rough women standing akimbo at street doors.

s.d: Of weapons, especially firearms: one held in each hand.
x: Although it was a little impractical, Elmer held his revolvers akimbo because to him it looked cool.

akin.e: From a corruption of of kin, from Middle English of kyn (“related, of kin”), equivalent to a- + kin (1550s). Compare Old English cyn, cynn (“akin, proper, suitable”, adj.).

s.d: (rare) To relate or compare; to liken.
x: I like to akin the P-Diddy case to Gen-Z's version of the O.J. Simpson trial.

s.d: similar in quality or character
related by blood
Of persons, of the same kin; related by blood.
x: [W]e are too near a kin to lye together, tho' vve may Lodge near one another; […]
The faces changed, passing in rotation. Youthful faces, bearded faces, dark faces: faces serene, or faces moody, but all akin with the brotherhood of the sea.

s.d: Allied by nature; similar; partaking of the same properties; of the same kind.
x: Is not then Fruition near akin to Love?
She told me that she hoped my Face was not akin to my Tongue.
